tests.procedure: Under strong white light check each received sample container separately in a clean transparent watch glass or glass dish for foreign particles, colour and conformity with the visual specification.

details.bpText: White or almost white, crystalline powder, colorless crystals or granules, efflorescent.

tests.procedure: Weigh 100 mg sample in a stoppered tube; add 0.1 mL solvent, shake 1 min, hold at 25.0 ± 0.5 °C for 15 min, repeat shake/hold once if not dissolved; stepwise add 0.9 mL, 2 mL, 7 mL solvent (same shake and hold) to classify very soluble / freely soluble / soluble / sparingly soluble; if still undissolved use 10 mg in 10 mL (slightly soluble) then 1 mg in 10 mL (very slightly soluble), else practically insoluble. Repeat with ethanol (96 per cent).

details.reference: BP (SC IV K.) Characters Section (Hygroscopicity and Solubility)

tests.procedure: Dissolve 1 g in 10 mL water; the solution is strongly acidic (< 4).

details.reference: BP Appendix V K. Approximate pH of Solutions

tests.procedure: IR identification: dry the sample and the reference at 105 ± 2 °C for 2 h; mix intimately with potassium bromide and compress into a transparent pellet; compare the spectrum with that of Citric Acid Monohydrate CRS.

details.reference: BP Appendix II A. Infrared Spectrophotometry

tests.procedure: Add about 5 mg of the substance to a mixture of 1 mL acetic anhydride and 3 mL pyridine; a red colour develops.
Dissolve 0.5 g in 5 mL water; neutralise with 1 M sodium hydroxide (about 7 mL); add 10 mL calcium chloride solution; heat to boiling; a white precipitate is formed.

details.reagent: 10 mL calcium chloride solution (7.35 g in 100 mL water)

tests.procedure: Appearance of solution: dissolve 2.0 g in water and dilute to 10 mL; the solution is clear and colourless or not more intensely coloured than reference solution Y7.

details.referenceSolution: Y7 (2.5 mL standard solution Y + 97.5 mL hydrochloric acid 10 g/L)
details.reference: BP Appendix IV A and IV B

tests.procedure: Readily carbonisable substances: 1.0 g in a clean test tube; add 10 mL sulfuric acid; heat immediately in a water bath at 90 ± 1 °C for 60 min; cool rapidly; the solution is not more intensely coloured than a mixture of 1 mL red primary solution and 9 mL yellow primary solution.

details.comparator: 1 mL red primary + 9 mL yellow primary solution

tests.procedure: Sulphates limit test (BP Appendix VII): to 4.5 mL sulfate standard solution (10 ppm SO4) R1 add 3 mL of 250 g/L barium chloride, shake, stand 1 min; to 2.5 mL of this suspension add 15 mL of the sample solution (2.0 g in water diluted to 30 mL) and 0.5 mL acetic acid (standard: 15 mL of 10 ppm SO4 solution). After 5 min any opalescence in the test solution is not more intense than the standard.

details.reference: BP Appendix VII Limit Tests, Sulfates

tests.procedure: Oxalic acid limit test (BP Appendix VII): test solution 0.80 g in 4 mL water, add 3 mL hydrochloric acid and 1 g zinc granules, boil 1 min, stand 2 min; transfer supernatant to 0.25 mL of 10 g/L phenyl hydrazine hydrochloride, boil, cool, add equal volume of hydrochloric acid and 0.25 mL of 50 g/L potassium ferricyanide, stand 30 min. Standard: 4 mL of 0.1 g/L oxalic acid treated the same way. Any pink colour in the test is not more intense than the standard.
Water content by calibrated Karl Fischer on 0.500 g sample.

details.reference: BP Appendix IX C. Determination of Water

tests.procedure: Sulphated ash (BP Appendix IX A): weigh empty crucible previously ignited at 600-650 °C and cooled in desiccator (W0); weigh 1.0 g sample (W1); moisten with a small amount of sulfuric acid, char gently on hot plate, moisten residue again, heat until white fumes cease; ignite in muffle at 600-650 °C, cool in desiccator, weigh (W2); repeat to constant weight. % = (W2 - W0) / (W1 - W0) x 100.

details.reference: BP Appendix IX A. Determination of Sulfated Ash

tests.procedure: Assay (BP, acid-base titration): dissolve 0.550 g in 50 mL water; titrate with 1 M sodium hydroxide using 0.5 mL phenolphthalein solution as indicator. 1 mL of 1 M sodium hydroxide = 64.03 mg C6H8O7. Assay = (E.P x eq.wt x F x 100 x 100) / (Wt x (100 - WC)) as printed.

details.titrantStandardization: 1.50 g potassium hydrogen phthalate in 50 mL water; 1 mL 1 M NaOH = 204.2 mg potassium hydrogen phthalate
details.equivalenceFactor: 1 mL of 1 M sodium hydroxide = 64.03 mg C6H8O7
details.formula: Assay = (E.P x eq.wt x F x 100 * 100) / Wt x (100 - WC); Wt in g; WC = water content
details.reference: BP 2024 Monograph for Citric Acid Monohydrate
